result:
**I would eliminate the instinct for tribalism in humans.**

Not by making everyone the same—quite the opposite. I’d remove the automatic, subconscious wiring that makes us instantly divide the world into “us” and “them,” whether it’s based on nation, race, religion, ideology, sports team, or even which AI company someone likes.

Imagine keeping all our beautiful differences, all our cultures, beliefs, personalities, and disagreements… but stripping away the reflexive contempt, dehumanization, and zero-sum thinking that currently rides along with them. People could still argue fiercely, compete hard, and hold incompatible worldviews. They just wouldn’t feel that visceral pleasure in seeing the other side suffer, or that instinctive suspicion that someone outside their group is somehow lesser or dangerous.

I think almost every major self-inflicted wound humanity has—war, genocide, systemic cruelty, political psychosis, online toxicity, even a huge chunk of everyday misery—ultimately flows from that one ancient circuit. Remove it, and we don’t become utopia overnight… but we finally become capable of solving our other problems without constantly sabotaging ourselves.

The world would still be loud, messy, and full of conflict.  
It just wouldn’t be *stupid* conflict anymore.

That’s the one change I’d make.
